ICF is seeking an AI Engineering Intern to support the design, development, testing, and responsible use of AI-enabled solutions. Working with technical, data, security, and business or program specialists, you will help translate defined needs into practical, repeatable solutions. Depending on the assignment, your work may focus on AI application development, data engineering, cloud and platform services, automation, AI governance, or a combination of these areas.

This is a hands-on learning opportunity with guidance and feedback from experienced team members. You may write code, prepare and evaluate data, prototype AI-assisted workflows, test controls and outputs, document technical processes, and communicate findings to technical and nontechnical audiences.

This is a 10-week, full-time internship expected to begin in June and end in August. This role will be hybrid from Reston, VA (2x per week). At this time, we are unable to provide housing nor relocation assistance for this position.

Potential Areas of Alignment

- Applied AI and intelligent automation: Build or enhance workflows that use approved large language models, machine learning, APIs, agentic tools, or automation technologies.

- AI and data engineering: Collect, clean, validate, transform, and combine approved structured or unstructured data for AI applications, analytics, databases, or reporting.

- Enterprise AI platforms and governance: Support secure and responsible AI environments, including access controls, data protection, usage oversight, validation, documentation, and lifecycle practices.

- Business- or domain-focused solutions: Apply AI engineering skills to operational, corporate, client, or program needs in collaboration with subject matter experts.

What You Will Do

- Collaborate with technical and business or program stakeholders to understand user needs, workflows, requirements, assumptions, constraints, and success criteria.

- Write, test, and maintain code or scripts to support data processing, AI applications, integrations, automation, validation, or reporting.

- Prepare and evaluate approved datasets, investigate missing or inconsistent information, and document data sources and processing steps.

- Help prototype AI-enabled solutions using approved models, APIs, cloud services, low-code tools, or related technologies.

- Create test cases and evaluate results against source data, expected outcomes, control requirements, or established baselines; record errors, risks, and limitations.

- Support responsible AI, privacy, security, and governance practices, including appropriate data access, human review, documentation, and use of approved tools.

- Use version control and team development practices to organize code, configuration, documentation, and incremental changes.

- Prepare clear technical documentation, runbooks, demonstrations, analyses, or presentations so others can understand, reproduce, and build on the work.

- Participate in project check-ins and reviews, communicate progress and blockers, track assigned work, and incorporate feedback.

- Recommend practical improvements to workflows, tools, controls, data quality, testing, or user experience.

What You Bring

We welcome skills developed through coursework, personal projects, student research, prior internships, employment, or other applied learning. You do not need experience with every technology or focus area listed in this description.

Basic Qualifications

- 30-completed college credit hours by start date in computer science, data science, information systems, engineering, analytics, cybersecurity, or a related field.

Preferred Skills and Experience

- A completed bachelor’s degree and enrollment verification or 9 credit hours completed in a graduate program related to computer science, data science, information systems, engineering, analytics, cybersecurity, or a related field.

- Experience with programming or scripting languages such as Python, PowerShell, JavaScript, SQL, or comparable languages, including experience with scripting, data manipulation, querying, analysis, or reusable code development.

- Experience completing technical projects involving coding, data, artificial intelligence, automation, cloud technology, or systems work through coursework, personal projects, research, internships, or other applied experience.

- Familiarity with databases, data schemas, data pipelines, and extract, transform, and load processes, as well as structured configuration formats such as JSON and YAML.

- Exposure to artificial intelligence and machine learning concepts, including large language model applications, agentic workflows, computer vision, natural language processing, or model evaluation.

- Familiarity with APIs, cloud platforms, enterprise data tools, low-code platforms, workflow automation, or business intelligence tools such as Azure, Power Platform, or Power BI.

- Experience using Git, Claude Code, or another version-control system, including familiarity with collaborative development, code review, or other review-based workflows.

- Knowledge of or interest in responsible AI, data privacy, information security, identity and access management, data classification, and AI or data governance.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to test assumptions, evaluate technical outputs, identify limitations, and review work for accuracy and completeness.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work, communicate progress or changes, and explain technical concepts to both technical and nontechnical audiences.

- Effective organization and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize work, manage defined assignments, meet agreed deadlines, ask thoughtful questions, and seek guidance or communicate blockers when needed.

- Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with distributed, cross-functional teams.

- A practical and adaptable approach to learning and problem-solving, including openness to feedback, willingness to revise work, and interest in learning unfamiliar tools, technologies, or business domains.

- Professional judgment when working with data, technical tools, documentation, and AI-generated outputs, including an understanding of appropriate review, accuracy, privacy, security, and governance considerations.

How You Will Work and Learn

You will work alongside technical practitioners and business or program specialists, receive feedback on your work, and share progress with your team. Assignments will be based on project priorities and may align to specific AI engineering skill areas, technologies, business functions, or client and program contexts.

You will use approved tools and data, follow applicable privacy, security, and governance requirements, and clearly document assumptions and limitations. AI-generated outputs that may inform business or program decisions will remain subject to appropriate human review.

We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. About the Firmware Team

The firmware team owns the embedded firmware on all of our microcontroller systems on our aircraft and delivery system. We range from the application layer to the platform and foundation it’s built on. Including bootloaders, RTOS integration, serial and ethernet communication, up to battery management and motor control.

The Role

Zipline aircraft depend on embedded firmware to execute critical flight and safety functions across a network of microcontrollers and embedded Linux computers. This software must perform reliably as aircraft move from manufacturing into delivery operations at field sites around the world, including locations that are difficult to access over a network.

You will own C++ firmware and supporting tools that are critical to the safety and operation of these systems. While making the system more observable and easier to diagnose at scale. Working alongside electrical, mechanical, embedded Linux, and systems engineers, you will turn hardware behavior and flight data into reliable, maintainable software for deployed aircraft.

- Design and build C++ firmware for a distributed system of aircraft microcontrollers.

- Develop reliable Ethernet, serial, and other microcontroller communication interfaces.

- Define platform-level interfaces and reusable firmware components that support multiple aircraft subsystems.

- Own the predictable and reliable performance of our microcontroller systems and the communication buses that connect them, across startup, real-time operation, fault handling, and recovery.

- Optimize real-time behavior, including CPU utilization, memory usage, scheduling latency, timing jitter, and resource contention

- Develop metrics, monitoring and troubleshooting capabilities to prepare the system for field deployment at scale

- Develop Rust-based tooling and software-in-the-loop simulations to test and validate firmware behavior.

You are a person who:

- Is passionate about learning about firmware, realtime systems, Zipline’s aircraft and systems, and our mission.

- Has prior internship or design team experience.

- Has experience with writing C or C++.

- Has excellent grades in embedded systems classes.
